item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Ukrainian forces are now conducting deep-strike operations up to 2,500 km, hitting targets such as a titanium plant 1,400 km from the border, a Tolyatti factory and a Krasnodar Krai airfield, while Russian forces continue drone and missile attacks on Ukrainian civilian sites, killing eight and injuring 51, including a residential building in Vinnytsia. Starlink speed restrictions have been lifted, restoring stable connectivity for Ukraine's military. Four people were killed in two drone attacks in Russia's Belgorod region. The conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israel is closing all West Bank land crossings on election day while expanding raids in Hebron that have forced thousands from their homes and led the IDF to forcibly remove 2,231 Palestinians from the city. Israeli airstrikes have hit a university campus in Gaza and a building in Nuseirat, killing three people, and separate strikes killed eight civilians including a child. The IDF is also targeting Hamas financing networks, reporting the killing of two terror operatives involved in funding the group. Visually and hearing-impaired children in Gaza are missing school because of the war. The conflict produced 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Ghana is working to prevent the war in Burkina Faso from spilling into its territory, reflecting regional concerns about the conflict's spread. The Supreme Court halted the appeal of a former minister sentenced for embezzlement, and a Cameroonian scholar has called for new peace talks with Anglophone separatists. item.title: Myanmar's civil war: the situation
item.description:
Aung San Suu Kyi spoke with her son for the first time in over five years, and he said she sounded fairly healthy, while military commander Min Aung Hlaing met Japan envoy Sasakawa, showing diplomatic engagement despite ongoing fighting. Military bombing in Sittwe left streets silent after dusk and caused air ticket prices to rise three to four times as many people fled to Yangon, while columns of troops moved around Pulin village and displaced civilians from 70 villages across three townships. A blast in the Rakhine state capital killed at least two people, and a bus crash in Mandalay region killed six and injured twelve.
